message.content:
Below are two ways you can spin‑up a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Note** – “EC2” is Amazon’s terminology. In Google Cloud the equivalent is a *Compute Engine* instance.  
>  Make sure you have:
>  * a GCP project (`PROJECT_ID`) with billing enabled  
>  * the **Compute Engine API** enabled  
>  * a service account or OAuth token with `compute.instances.create` scope  
>  * the `gcloud` CLI installed (or use the REST API directly)

---

## 1️⃣  gcloud CLI

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata=startup-script='#!/bin/bash
    apt-get update
    apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
    reboot' \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM allocation |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk |
| `--accelerator` | Attach one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--metadata` | Optional startup script to install NVIDIA drivers |
| `--tags` | Allow HTTP/HTTPS traffic (if you plan to expose services) |

> **Tip** – If you need more GPUs or a different machine type, adjust `--machine-type` and `count=` accordingly.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON body)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., from a script or CI pipeline), use the following JSON payload:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nreboot"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### POST request

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

Replace `@instance.json` with the path to the JSON file above, and adjust `my-gcp-project`, `us-central1-a`, and other fields as needed.

---

## 3️⃣  Quick sanity check

After creation, verify the GPU is attached:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=my-gcp-project \
  --zone=us-central1-a \
  --format="get(accelerators)"
```

You should see something like:

```
[{'acceleratorType': 'projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000', 'acceleratorCount': 1}]
```

---

### Common pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **GPU quota exceeded** | Request a quota increase in the GCP console under *IAM & Admin → Quotas*. |
| **Instance fails to start** | Ensure the zone supports GPUs (`us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`, etc.). |
| **Driver not installed** | The startup script installs `nvidia-driver-535`. If you need a newer driver, change the package name. |
| **Billing disabled** | Instances won’t launch if billing isn’t enabled for the project. |

---

That’s it! You now have a ready‑to‑use Compute Engine instance with an RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. Happy computing!
